lessons.title: Installation, CLI, and your first program
lessons.description: Pin the release, choose the VM, and learn the command boundaries.

lessons.title: Bindings, values, and mutability
lessons.description: Use let, mut, and const according to Kujo’s actual rules.
lessons.reason: Mutation through an immutable binding is rejected.

lessons.title: Values, operators, and truthiness
lessons.description: Predict boolean results, checked arithmetic, and equality.
lessons.reason: The operands are valid integers but their sum exceeds the signed 64-bit range. The runtime must reject overflow rather than wrap silently.

lessons.title: Control flow and block scopes
lessons.description: Make decisions, terminate loops, and keep iteration state local.
lessons.reason: A never-declared name is a runtime error. The separate scope probe records the release discrepancy.

lessons.title: Functions, callbacks, and return values
lessons.description: Extract decisions into small functions with explicit results.
lessons.reason: The function requires two positional arguments. The failure concerns arity, not the arithmetic inside the function.

lessons.title: Collections, pipes, and null handling
lessons.description: Transform structured data without hiding missing-value errors.
lessons.reason: The missing dictionary key throws before null coalescing can select a fallback.

lessons.title: Scope, shadowing, and capture
lessons.description: Locate state by lexical binding, then test capture assumptions.
lessons.reason: Two declarations target the same lexical scope. This is a duplicate declaration, not valid shadowing.

lessons.title: Structs and enums
lessons.description: Model domain records and states before adding behavior.
lessons.reason: Runtime structs are not directly JSON-serializable; select a dictionary of fields.

lessons.title: Match, Result, and Option
lessons.description: Give expected failure and absence their own states.
lessons.reason: An out-of-bounds lookup is a runtime error, not automatically None. Wrap an explicit bounds decision in an Option-returning function when absence is part of your API.

lessons.title: Exceptions and recoverable errors
lessons.description: Catch failures at the boundary that can make a decision.
lessons.reason: No exception boundary handles this deliberate failure, so the command must fail.

lessons.title: Optional typing without imaginary guarantees
lessons.description: Use annotations while respecting dynamic VM execution.
lessons.reason: The runtime operation receives an incompatible dictionary. This demonstrates dynamic execution failure, not a static type-check guarantee.

lessons.title: Async functions and await
lessons.description: Own pending work and inspect its completion.
lessons.reason: The awaited operation rejects. Completion must propagate the failure rather than produce a success receipt.

lessons.title: Spawn and bounded concurrent work
lessons.description: Choose owned results over timing assumptions.
lessons.reason: A failed worker must make the awaited batch fail. Do not accept a partial batch as a complete result.

lessons.title: Modules and explicit exports
lessons.description: Separate reusable code from entrypoint effects.
lessons.reason: The requested module does not exist in the configured roots. This is a resolution failure, not a provider installation request.

lessons.title: Projects, packages, and lockfiles
lessons.description: Reproduce a manifest without inventing a public registry.
lessons.reason: This small assertion illustrates the invariant. The real package drift failure is additionally exercised and recorded by the package integration gate; a string comparison is not a substitute for that gate.

lessons.title: Finding the standard library contract
lessons.description: Look up arity, result shape, failure, and authority before calling.
lessons.reason: The text is malformed JSON. The native parser returns a real parse-location failure instead of silently producing empty data.

lessons.title: Testing, fixtures, and runtime evidence
lessons.description: Make failures intentional and success independently checkable.
lessons.reason: This intentionally incorrect expectation must fail. A verifier that accepts it cannot establish correctness.

lessons.title: Diagnostics and machine-readable interfaces
lessons.description: Serve humans and agents from one explicit result contract.
lessons.reason: Run this with --json-runtime-diagnostics as an additional drill. JSON on stdout must not override the nonzero failure exit.

lessons.title: Documentation as a build artifact
lessons.description: Generate API evidence and write the decisions extraction cannot infer.
lessons.reason: The call violates the documented input boundary. Keeping a failing usage drill beside docs helps reveal examples that cannot actually run.

lessons.title: Editor integration and the LSP boundary
lessons.description: Keep tooling connected to the same language contract.
lessons.reason: The malformed parameter list is diagnosed without executing a program. Compare CLI checking with LSP diagnostics on this same source.

lessons.title: Filesystem automation with bounded paths
lessons.description: Read intended inputs and make writes deliberate.
lessons.reason: The relative path tries to escape the selected root. Filesystem-read authority is granted, so rejection should concern path containment.

lessons.title: Processes without unnecessary shells
lessons.description: Use argv, bounded output, and an explicit result receipt.
lessons.reason: The argv array is empty. The call must reject invalid arguments before starting a child process.

lessons.title: HTTP and network boundaries
lessons.description: Separate response handling from live transport.
lessons.reason: This drill has no network-client allowance. It must fail at the capability boundary before any socket is useful. The project integration gate tests real local HTTP separately.

lessons.title: Structured data and local persistence
lessons.description: Store explicit schemas and keep migrations inspectable.
lessons.reason: The persisted representation is malformed. Loading must reject it rather than return an apparently empty state.

lessons.title: Trusted execution and minimum authority
lessons.description: Prove a denial, grant one effect, and test the remaining boundary.
lessons.reason: The lesson grants read authority only. A write must still be denied; the gate must not create the target file.

lessons.title: Secrets, redaction, and endpoint policy
lessons.description: Keep credential values out of ordinary output.
lessons.reason: reveal deliberately returns the inner value. The failed assertion demonstrates why revealing before logging defeats the wrapper.

lessons.title: AI effects and portable messages
lessons.description: Treat model responses as uncertain external input.
lessons.reason: This call has no AI capability allowance. Constructing messages is pure, but making the AI request is an effect.

lessons.title: Deterministic request identity
lessons.description: Know which work a cassette or cache entry represents.
lessons.reason: The prompts represent different work, so the deliberately equal-hash expectation fails.

lessons.title: Record, replay, and offline evidence
lessons.description: Make AI integration tests independent of a live provider.
lessons.reason: The changed request has no cassette. Strict mode must report replay_miss and must not contact the endpoint.

lessons.title: Streaming and cancellation
lessons.description: Distinguish delivered chunks from a completed domain result.
lessons.reason: The callback is not callable. The runtime must reject the invalid callback contract.

lessons.title: Structured outputs and schema validation
lessons.description: Parse text, validate shape, then evaluate meaning.
lessons.reason: The string is valid JSON-like data but violates the required integer type. The acceptance assertion must fail.

lessons.title: Context budgets, embeddings, and vectors
lessons.description: Bound context and keep retrieval policy outside core math.
lessons.reason: The vectors have different dimensions. Ranking and similarity require compatible numeric shapes.

lessons.title: Bounded AI tool loops
lessons.description: Validate a proposed call before supplying a tool result.
lessons.reason: Zero is not a valid finite step budget for this API. The invalid options must reject before a request is useful.

lessons.title: Mechanism versus policy
lessons.description: Compose an application without turning the language into a framework.
lessons.reason: The attempt budget is exhausted. A policy that still accepts another attempt would violate the bound.

lessons.title: Loop Engineering, specs, and stop conditions
lessons.description: Turn an open-ended request into bounded work.
lessons.reason: The proposed execution budget permits no valid attempt. Reject the spec before starting work.

lessons.title: Evaluation independent of generation
lessons.description: Reject plausible but wrong output with observable criteria.
lessons.reason: The proposal has the right shape but the wrong factual count. Independent evaluation rejects it.

lessons.title: Evidence, run records, and work boundaries
lessons.description: Leave enough proof for the next person or program.
lessons.reason: The receipt claims PASS without passing evaluation. A status label cannot replace evidence.

lessons.title: Isolation, observability, and watchdogs
lessons.description: Control the host and detect failures outside the happy path.
lessons.reason: The observed attempt count exceeds policy. A watchdog must report a violation rather than normalize it away.

lessons.title: MCP and external tool interoperability
lessons.description: Expose a schema without confusing discovery with authority.
lessons.reason: The extra argument is outside the tool schema. Discovery metadata must not allow arbitrary execution parameters.
